results.description: Like Barnabas, you are the person who sees the best in others and fights for their potential. You are the bridge-builder, the advocate, the one who speaks up for the person everyone else has dismissed. Your generosity is not limited to money — you are generous with your time, your trust, and your reputation. You gladly decrease so others can increase, and your greatest joy comes from watching someone you believed in fulfill their calling. The church could not function without people like you, even though your contribution is rarely celebrated.
strengths: Seeing and drawing out potential in others
Building bridges between people and communities
Generosity with resources, trust, and encouragement
Willingness to take risks on untested people
watchFor: Avoiding necessary conflict to maintain peace
Being taken advantage of by those who exploit your generosity
Struggling with resentment if the people you champion surpass and forget you
Difficulty confronting sin or failure in people you have invested in

scripture.text: When he arrived and saw what the grace of God had done, he was glad and encouraged them all to remain true to the Lord with all their hearts. He was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith, and a great number of people were brought to the Lord.

results.title: The Faithful Chronicler
results.description: Like Luke, you are the person who stays. Your gifts may not be the most visible — you are the researcher, the writer, the careful thinker, the behind-the-scenes supporter — but they are among the most lasting. You bring order to chaos, clarity to confusion, and loyalty to relationships. When everyone else has moved on to the next exciting thing, you are still faithfully doing the work that needs to be done. Your greatest ministry may be your consistent presence in someone's life during their darkest season.
strengths: Deep loyalty and commitment to people and projects
Careful, thorough approach to understanding truth
Ability to communicate clearly and preserve important stories
Steady presence that others can depend on in every season
watchFor: Hiding behind research or preparation to avoid stepping out in faith
Undervaluing your gifts because they are not 'up front'
Difficulty asking for help or expressing your own needs
Tendency to observe life rather than fully engaging in it

scripture.text: With this in mind, since I myself have carefully investigated everything from the beginning, I too decided to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus, so that you may know the certainty of the things you have been taught.

results.title: The Worship Warrior
results.description: Like Silas, you bring the song to the prison cell. You have a God-given ability to find praise in the darkest circumstances, and your worship is not performance — it is warfare. You thrive in partnership, drawing strength from fellow believers and multiplying courage through community. Your faith is most visible not in the good times but in the midnight hours when everything has gone wrong and you still choose to sing. People around you are watching, even when you do not realize it — and your defiant joy in suffering points them to a God who is bigger than any chain.
strengths: Ability to worship authentically in suffering
Strength in partnership and team ministry
Courage that is contagious in dark circumstances
Prophetic encouragement that strengthens others' faith
watchFor: Discouragement when community breaks down or partners leave
Using positivity to avoid processing legitimate grief or pain
Difficulty functioning alone — needing a partner to feel effective
Frustration when others do not match your level of faith in hard times

scripture.text: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them. Suddenly there was such a violent earthquake that the foundations of the prison were shaken. At once all the prison doors flew open, and everyone's chains came loose.
